thread:
lina (Docs): Note: releasing Python SDK v2.0.0-rc1 today. Big picture: async-first APIs, renamed callsites, and a deprecation schedule for the sync client. Please review the migration guide and examples.

owen (SDK): Summary: new package layout redwood.async_client.AsyncClient, old Client.sync methods removed from primary docs, generate() -> text_generate(). We're also enabling streaming with async iterators by default.

oj ci-bot: Release published to PyPI: redwood==2.0.0rc1; docs site updated at https://docs.redwood.inference/sdk/python/v2/async.

jana (Support): Will customers on older runtimes be impacted? Any notes for our triage playbook?

owen (SDK): Customers on Python <3.8 won't be able to use the async client — we added a compatibility note and a short-term shim package redwood-compat for sync apps. Deprecation timeline: sync client deprecated now, removal planned for v3.0 (~6 months).

felix (DevEx): Action items for DevEx: add migration snippets to quickstarts repo, prepare a sample PR converting 5 top examples to async, and schedule a migration office hours.

lina (Docs): I'll add a clear banner on legacy pages, a FAQ section for performance expectations, and a one-page checklist for engineers migrating monoliths. Please flag any missing edge-case examples.

owen (SDK): One note: async brings batching + KV cache benefits that can reduce token cost in high-volume flows. We'll include benchmark numbers in the guide.

lina (Docs): Thanks — please drop any suggested wording here or open a PR against docs.
